title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.78): S is a base scheme, X→S a smooth proper relative curve, T⊂X a divisor finite étale over S, and U=X∖T. One component of T is a section i_0 (ξ) of T over S. There is an extension 1→π→E_U→E_S→1. Here E_U=π_1(U), E_S=π_1(S), and π is the geometric fibre group, completed prime to the residue characteristics. The p.78 remark that one needs π_2(S)→π_1(fibre) to be zero is what makes this sequence exact on the left.

The cusp i gives a π-conjugacy class of inertia subgroups L_i≅Ẑ(1) in π. Because the cusp is defined over S, this conjugacy class is E_U-stable. A Frattini-type 'general argument' then gives E_U=π·N(L_i), so the normalizer N(L_i) maps onto E_S. For hyperbolic fibres the cuspidal inertia is self-normalizing in π (N_π(L_i)=L_i). Hence the extension (13): 1→T→N(L_i)→E_S→1, with T=Ẑ(1)=lim μ_n and E_S acting through the cyclotomic character. N(L_i) is the 'cuspidal decomposition group'.

Its isomorphism class is c_i∈H^2(E_S,Ẑ(1)) (14). If S is an étale K(π,1), for instance an elementary (Artin) neighbourhood in characteristic 0, then (15) H^2(E_S,Ẑ(1))≅H^2_et(S,Ẑ(1))=lim H^2(S,μ_n).

The Kummer sequence gives (16): 0→Pic(S)/n→H^2(S,μ_n)→Br(S)[n]→0. Passing to the limit gives (17): 0→Pic(S)^→H^2(S,Ẑ(1))→T Br(S)=lim_n Br(S)[n]. The marginal note reads Pic^ := lim Pic/n (= Pic⊗Ẑ when Pic is finitely generated).

Next page: over a finitely generated field of characteristic 0, Pic(S) is finitely generated (Mordell–Weil–Néron), so Pic(S)→H^2(S,Ẑ(1)) is injective. Grothendieck then claims that c_i is the Chern class of the normal (or conormal) bundle of the section ξ in X. Proof sketch: replace X by its formal completion along ξ(S), i.e. a tubular neighbourhood. Read (13) as the homotopy exact sequence of the punctured neighbourhood, which is a G_m-torsor over S, so its class is c_1 of the normal bundle.

Purpose: to understand the obstruction to splitting the cuspidal decomposition group over a base. This is the obstruction to tangential base points / cuspidal sections in families, within the anabelian 'Longue Marche' programme for relative curves over elementary bases.
errors: Notational clash: T denotes both the cusp divisor (U=X∖T) and Ẑ(1)=lim μ_n.
The kernel of N(L_i)→E_S equals L_i only if L_i is self-normalizing in π. This needs the fibre to be hyperbolic; it fails e.g. for G_m, where π is abelian. This is not stated.
H^2(E_S,Ẑ(1))=lim H^2(E_S,μ_n) needs continuous cohomology plus a Mittag-Leffler or finiteness condition on the H^1 terms. This is implicitly assumed.
Pic^=lim Pic/n coincides with Pic⊗Ẑ only when Pic is finitely generated. The marginal '=' is fine only under the next page's hypothesis.
The prime-to-residue-characteristic restriction is mentioned but only half-written, so it is left vague.

ideas.what: Normalizer of the cuspidal inertia subgroup surjects onto π_1(S), giving an extension of π_1(S) by Ẑ(1) (cuspidal decomposition group over a base)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Mochizuki, Stix, among others)
ideas.where_published: implicit in Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche discussions of tangential base points

ideas.what: Identification H^2(π_1(S),Ẑ(1))≅H^2_et(S,Ẑ(1)) for S an étale K(π,1)
ideas.modern_name: K(π,1) property of Artin elementary neighbourhoods

ideas.what: Limit of the Kummer sequences: 0→Pic^→H^2(S,Ẑ(1))→T Br(S)
ideas.modern_name: ℓ-adic/Ẑ Kummer sequence, Tate module of the Brauer group
ideas.where_published: Dix exposés: Le groupe de Brauer

ideas.what: Extension class of the cuspidal decomposition group equals the Chern class of the (co)normal bundle of the cusp section; proof via the punctured formal neighbourhood viewed as a G_m-torsor
ideas.modern_name: obstruction to relative tangential base points = c_1(normal bundle) (ψ-class in the universal case)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; used e.g. by Hain for universal curves (tangential base points over M_{g,n})

missed.claim: Explicit statement that the cuspidal decomposition extension over a K(π,1) base is classified by c_1 of the normal bundle of the cusp section in Pic(S)^⊂H^2(S,Ẑ(1)). Combined with Mordell–Weil–Néron injectivity, this gives a criterion for the existence of relative tangential sections. The statement is early and precise, but the fact itself is essentially folklore today.
missed.quote: La classe d'isomorphie est un élément (14) c_i ∈ H^2(E_S, T) ... que je me propose d'étudier
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a relevant precursor for the section conjecture over higher-dimensional bases and for 'packets' of cuspidal sections in families (ψ-classes in the anabelian setting). It is probably not new to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, correct computation linking cuspidal decomposition groups in families to Picard/Chern classes via Kummer theory. The idea is natural and known in folklore and later literature (e.g. Hain), so it is notable mainly as an unpublished Grothendieck detail.
transcription_corrections: 'des scindages[?] par cette extension' is more likely 'des extensions de E_S par T' or a similar phrase; the sense is that N(L_i) is an extension of E_S by T.
In (17) the last term is lim_n {}_nH^2(S,G_m), i.e. the Tate module of Br(S).
The marginal note under (17) reads 'def = lim Pic/n (= Pic ⊗ ...)', defining Pic(S)^.
The final line reads 'Dans le cas où S est un schéma élémentaire sur un corps de car. 0 de type fini [sur] Q', continued on the next page.
